qc.label_under_test: A label handed back between two people: one person labels another (sees him as a tyrant, calls him a bore, considers him reckless) and then that other person labels the first in return (and he sees me as a slacker); it fires on the returned label's opening ('me', 'as', 'a', 'like'), friendly or hostile labels alike, with or without a sentence introducing the pair. A plain tit-for-tat with no label (I hate him and he hates me), a one-way label, or two people labelling the same third party stays quiet, and it is weak when the narrator is labelled first and answers back.

neighbours.label: A label handed back between two people: one person labels another (sees him as a tyrant, calls him a bore, considers him reckless) and then that other person labels the first in return (and he sees me as a slacker); it fires on the returned label's opening ('me', 'as', 'a', 'like'), friendly or hostile labels alike, with or without a sentence introducing the pair. A plain tit-for-tat with no label (I hate him and he hates me), a one-way label, or two people labelling the same third party stays quiet, and it is weak when the narrator is labelled first and answers back.
fire: I see my boss as a tyrant, and he sees me as a slacker.
She calls him a bore, and he calls her a snob.
My brother and I never got along: I considered him reckless, and he considered me a coward.
I think of Dana as a genius, and she thinks of me as a mentor.
To me he was a dreamer, and to him I was a cynic.
The two neighbours have feuded for years; Mr. Hale regards Mrs. Ortiz as a busybody, and she regards him as a grump.
I always saw my grandfather as a hero, and he saw me as his little partner in crime.
Tom treats his coach like a drill sergeant, and the coach treats him like a spoiled kid.
quiet: I can't stand my boss, and he can't stand me.
She calls him a bore, and he just shrugs and keeps talking.
My brother and I never got along: I avoided him, and he avoided me.
I think of Dana as a genius, and so does everyone in the lab.
To me he was a dreamer, and to my mother he was a dreamer too.
The two neighbours have feuded for years; Mr. Hale ignores Mrs. Ortiz, and she ignores him right back.
I always saw my grandfather as a hero, and he loved telling me stories every summer.
Tom and his coach both treat the new referee like a drill sergeant.

predictions: Blind test (sentences written by a label-only author). Expect most fire items 0.2-0.5 at the returned label; 'To me he was a dreamer' and the 'like' items may be weaker. Neighbours (L33/N5132- Apache-license paren, others failed) give no reason to change the label.
